Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testIntersectionNotIntersecting` calls `SubLine.intersection()` on two SubLines that do not intersect. The `SubLine.intersection(SubLine, boolean)` method tries to compute the intersection point between the underlying infinite lines via `line.intersection(subLine.line)`. This method uses `Line.closestPoint(Line)` which returns the closest point on the first line to the second line, or null if they are parallel or disjoint.

After computing this point `v1D`, `SubLine.intersection()` converts it to 1D subspace coordinates and checks if it lies within the 'remaining region' of each SubLine by calling `remainingRegion.checkPoint(line.toSubSpace(v1D))`. However, when the input lines do not actually intersect, the `line.intersection` returns null, leading to `v1D` being null. This results in a NullPointerException in `line.toSubSpace(v1D)` as it does not handle a null argument, as shown in `Line.toSubSpace()`.

Thus, the bug arises because `SubLine.intersection()` does not check if the intersection vector `v1D` returned by `line.intersection()` is null before calling methods on it, leading to an NPE when lines do not intersect.

The current bug report aligns with this: it mentions an NPE in `Line.toSubSpace()` due to non-intersecting input lines. The fix should add a null check on the intersection point before proceeding.

The recent reports do not add relevant insight as they focus on unrelated matrix or naming issues.

Steps to fix:
- In `SubLine.intersection(SubLine, boolean)`, add a check after `Vector3D v1D = line.intersection(subLine.line)` to return null immediately if v1D is null, preventing any downstream NullPointerException.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
